name: Panicum

project_scope.note: B009 Panicum set; P. coloratum is retained only as an introduced/invasive comparison.

study_strategy.warning: Do not identify these from a generic open panicle alone. Read the base, ligule/collar, leaf texture and panicle architecture together.
overlap_cautions: Open panicles occur in several species; inspect base, collar and mature spikelets together.
Master Plant Pool Panicum obtusum is a legacy concept corresponding to Hopia obtusa; do not add a fifth canonical Panicum card.
P. coloratum retains existing introduced/non-native comparison classification; no new range decision.

quick_key.if: Tall many-culmed rhizomatous perennial + TRIANGULAR white blade-base hair tuft and short fringed membranous ligule + very broad AWNLESS open panicle
Smaller glaucous stiff bunch + mostly basal leaves + shorter panicle with stiff ascending branches
Hairy ANNUAL with no enduring rhizomatous crown + huge irregular 'tumbleweed' panicle
Introduced African perennial + knotty tufted basal crown, shorter finer seedhead, no characteristic big switchgrass rhizome stand

curation_status.status: Four Panicum species in the genus comparison; source-installed switchgrass collar and spikelet macros take priority; rhizome/membrane contour remain honest photo gaps
curation_status.switchgrass_photo_upgrade: 2 real CC BY-SA 4.0 macros; 6 visible-point arrows; no taxonomy or nativity edits

fast_fill_note: All three PASS native Panicum learner pages in the current genus set now have 3-image FAST-FILL galleries. Panicum coloratum remains an introduced/target-zone FAIL comparison and is deliberately excluded from native fast-fill coverage.
look_here_first: When a grass looks like switchgrass, don't stop at the giant open panicle. OPEN ONE MATURE COLLAR: P. virgatum shows a dense triangular WHITE HAIR patch on the upper blade base and a short ciliate membrane, with NO true auricles. Then inspect the very OPEN BRANCHED pyramid of many tiny AWNLESS singly pedicelled spikelets and the rhizomatous perennial crown. In the other installed Panicums: P. hallii is shorter, often BLUE-GLAUCOUS, stiffly tufted with a modest panicle; P. capillare is an ANNUAL with hairs over much of its nodes/sheaths and an immense chaotic haze of panicle branches; P. coloratum is introduced African KLEINGRASS with tufted/knotty crown and a finer panicle. At larger-grass level, Indiangrass S. nutans differs in a prominent notched MEMBRANOUS 'rifle-sight' collar, golden narrower plume and BENT AWNS. Johnsongrass may have an open panicle but has different paired spikelets/rhizomes. Avoid cultivars or ornamental color as an identification standard.
shared_genus_traits: Jointed grass culms with leaf sheaths, collars and ligules.
Branched panicles of small spikelets; mature spikelet and glume/lemma details help resolve look-alikes.
Growth base, collar hairs and inflorescence branching distinguish these four learner species better than flower color.

comparison_cards.title: Switchgrass versus Indiangrass and Johnsongrass — collar, awn, spikelet pairing
comparison_cards.look_here_first: At blade base: Switchgrass WHITE TRIANGULAR hair cluster with short ciliate membrane. Indiangrass prominent upright pointed RIFLE-SIGHT membranous ligule. Johnsongrass normally broader developed smooth membrane with no switchgrass hair triangle. Then check seedhead: switchgrass broad airy panicle, individual AWNLESS small singly pedicelled spikelets; Indiangrass narrower golden awned plume with naked sterile pedicels; Johnsongrass pairs developed pedicelled spikelets with sessile units.

field_matrix.switchgrass: Triangular white hairs, short ciliate membrane; no true auricles
field_matrix.indiangrass: Tall stiff membrane with notched upright corners ('rifle sight')

field_matrix.switchgrass: Single ovoid ~3–5 mm AWNLESS unit on pedicel
field_matrix.indiangrass: AWNED fertile sessile spikelet + naked sterile pedicel
field_matrix.johnsongrass: Sessile fertile plus developed pedicelled spikelet

photo_requirements: Actual switchgrass blade-base WHITE HAIR COLLAR at mm scale
Actual switchgrass panicle branch and ovoid AWNLESS spikelets
Licensed Indiangrass membranous collar photo already in Sorghastrum lesson

comparison_cards.caution: The switchgrass membrane may be partly hidden by the hairs. Do not call the hair tuft a triangular membrane, and do not diagnose purely by a broad panicle.

comparison_cards.title: Switchgrass versus Hall's panicgrass, Witchgrass, and Kleingrass
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Start with LIFE CYCLE and BASE: large scaly-rhizomatous native perennial switchgrass, small glaucous stiff-tufted Hall's, hairy annual witchgrass, knotty introduced African kleingrass. Then examine blade-base hair patch and OPEN panicle branch scale.

field_matrix.virgatum: Spreading scaly rhizomes / many tall stems
Dense white TRIANGLE at upper blade base
field_matrix.hallii: Often much less distinctive; short fringe
field_matrix.coloratum: Variable hairs, not same strong paired trait

comparison_cards.caution: Environmental stress alters height and panicle spread; use reproductive spikelet and actual perennial basal structures together. P. coloratum stays introduced.

visual_comparison.title: Panicum crew field key — start on switchgrass collar then flowering spikelets
visual_comparison.subtitle: Six genus visual panels, with two exact switchgrass CC BY-SA macro plates and six real-structure arrow markers first. Installed and audited; no new speculative photo claims.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: SWITCHGRASS = WHITE HAIR TRIANGLE + AIRY PYRAMID + AWNLESS spikelets. HALL'S = short blue bunch. WITCHGRASS = hairy annual chaos. KLEINGRASS = introduced knotty bunch.

items.label: 1 · Switchgrass — ACTUAL ligule and white silky collar hairs
items.creator: Stefan.lefnaer
items.image_role: Real source-labeled ligule/collar close-up, SILKY fringe and physical 5 mm scale (membrane edge not individually scored)
items.caption: Stefan.lefnaer photographed a real P. virgatum blade–sheath junction with a 5-mm scale. The white fringe is the hairy collar/ligule region; do NOT call the hairs Indiangrass's stiff pointed rifle-sight membrane. The thin inner membrane is partly obscured, so no definitive membrane-tip arrow is claimed.
items.why_it_matters: Allows the crew to recognize and physically locate the main vegetative clue before flowering.
items.annotation_status: Original source visually reviewed; arrow endpoints target actual hairs, scale, individual spikelet/stigma and visible rachis; no invisible membrane tip claimed. Owner mobile QA pending.

items.label: 2 · Switchgrass — ACTUAL panicle spikelets, feathery stigmas, no awns
items.creator: Stefan.lefnaer
items.image_role: Actual Panicum panicle branch, awnless spikelets and visible plumose flowering stigmas, with 5 mm scale
items.caption: True source-labeled Panicum virgatum side branch at the 5-mm scale: individual green ovoid spikelets attach to thin pedicels; dark purple FEATHERY flowering structures are visible (stigmas, not bent awns). We don't claim that tiny glume edges or a mature seed anatomy are separately resolved.
items.why_it_matters: These are singly borne, awnless spikelets rather than the long twisted-awns and naked sterile pedicels of Indiangrass.
